tech-news.headline: Claude traces the secret origin of the NIST ECDSA curve seeds, the top AI story on Hacker News, as DeepSeek ships V4.1 Flash 1017 under MIT.
tech-news.note: Reddit was skipped because the Composio tools did not load in this run, and the Hacker News front?day=2026-10-17 page failed, so the live front page was used instead.

items.title: Claude finds how NSA generated the NIST ECDSA curve seeds
items.body: An Anthropic internal research model found the origin of the seeds for P-192 to P-521 in under half an hour. The seeds came from the C library lrand48 generator, seeded with Unix timestamps from 1997-1998, not from a hashed passphrase. Anthropic says this is not a cryptographic break and makes a backdoor less plausible. The $36,864 bounty goes to the Internet Security Research Group.
items.why: It shows what a frontier Claude model can do on a long, open-ended investigation task that humans failed to crack.

items.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 lands with MIT weights and 1M context
items.body: DeepSeek released V4.1 Flash 1017 on October 17 on its app, API (model ID deepseek-flash), Hugging Face and OpenRouter. It is a MoE model with 1M context and 384K max output. DeepSeek reports Terminal-Bench 4.0 at 42.3, up from 31.2. Price stays at $0.15 to $0.30 input and $0.60 to $1.20 output per million tokens.
items.why: It is a very cheap, open-weight coding model with an Anthropic-compatible API, so you can test it behind agent tools that expect the Claude API.

items.title: How the Claude Code team reviews 30,000 daily changes
items.body: Claude writes about 90% of Claude Code's code, so the team uses parallel AI bug-hunting agents, blocking security review and risk-tiered human approval. Low-risk PRs need no human after checks pass; high-risk PRs need two people. A three-round cap and diff-only re-review cut PRs needing five or more rounds from 8.9% to 1.5%. Code Review is now GA for Team and Enterprise, with /code-review for local use.
items.why: It gives a ready playbook for AI code review gates, risk tiers and CLAUDE.md/REVIEW.md feedback loops that you can copy into your own CI pipelines.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.302 turns on fork subagents by default
items.body: Version 2.1.302 enables fork subagents (subagent_type fork) by default in claude -p, the Agent SDK, the desktop app and VS Code. It adds CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_MODEL to pick the auto mode classifier model. The Read tool now refuses image sources over 128 MB. A fix stops plugin marketplaces re-cloning on every refresh with the git reftable format.
items.why: Fork subagents now run by default in claude -p and the Agent SDK, which changes how your headless agent jobs split work.

items.title: Claude Mythos 5 designs quantum circuits beating published records
items.body: Claude Mythos 5 designed circuits for eight primitives and used fewer qubits and gates than the best published designs. One elliptic-curve point addition design uses 17x fewer gates after a 53-hour run. A Reed-Solomon decoder for DQI uses about 12x fewer gates. The work involved Harvard and QuEra researchers.
items.why: It shows a practical closed-loop pattern: give Claude a spec and an automated evaluator, then let it iterate without humans.

items.title: Apple runs 816B Muse Spark Open across four Mac Studios
items.body: Apple ran Muse Spark Open (816B total, 42B active, NVFP4) across four M5 Ultra Mac Studios over RDMA on Thunderbolt 5. Tensor parallelism on four machines reached 36.73 tokens per second decode with 4.8 s time to first token. Two machines gave 24.99 tokens per second with tensor parallelism and 15.74 with pipeline parallelism. M5 Ultra decodes about 1.6x faster than M3 Ultra.
items.why: It gives real numbers for running a frontier-size open model locally with MLX tensor parallelism.
items.source: Apple Machine Learning Research, Hacker News 335 points

items.title: Mercor: AI benchmarks miss 90% of US working hours
items.body: Mercor mapped 29 agentic benchmarks to 18,797 O*NET tasks across 923 occupations. Only 208 occupations have a task covered by 5 or more benchmark prompts. Coverage favours AI-exposed and high-wage tasks. The authors call the results provisional.
items.why: It warns that benchmark scores say little about most real work, so you must build your own evals for your agent tasks.

tech-pulse.headline: Claude traced the origin of the NIST ECDSA curve seeds, and Hacker News made it the top story of the day.
tech-pulse.note: Reddit was skipped because the Composio tools were not available in this run; the HN 'front?day' page failed to load, and GitHub Trending returned stale data, so all items come from the live HN front page.

items.title: Claude explains the origin of NIST ECDSA curve seeds
items.body: Anthropic researchers worked with Claude on the seed values of the NIST elliptic curves P-192 to P-521. Claude found that the seeds came from the lrand48 random number generator, seeded with Unix timestamps. The team recovered the generator states with lattice reduction. They say this is not a cryptographic break, and it makes a hidden backdoor less plausible.
items.why: It shows Claude doing real security research, and the NIST curves protect the TLS and KMS keys in your AWS stack.

items.title: How the Claude Code team reviews code with agents
items.body: The Claude Code team moved most code reading to automated checks. Claude runs tests and linters, a parallel-agent review with voting filters findings, and a blocking security review runs before merge. A risk classifier sets human approval to zero, one or two people. From June to September, merged PRs more than doubled and the revert rate fell by over 40%.
items.why: You can copy this review pipeline for your own repos: Claude review, security gate, risk-based human approval.

items.title: Study: AI benchmarks miss 90% of US work hours
items.body: Mercor mapped prompts from 29 agentic benchmarks to 18,797 O*NET tasks across 923 occupations with an LLM judge. Only 208 occupations have a covered task. About 90% of US working hours go to tasks with little or no benchmark coverage. Mercor calls the results provisional.
items.why: It tells you which agent benchmarks match real tasks, so you can judge model claims for DevOps work.

items.title: Apple runs 816B Muse Spark Open on Mac Studio cluster
items.body: Apple ML Research ran Muse Spark Open, a mixture-of-experts model with 816B total and 42B active parameters, with MLX. It uses 4-bit NVFP4 on Mac Studio M5 Ultra machines with up to 512GB memory. MLX splits the model by pipeline or tensor parallelism over RDMA on Thunderbolt 5. Four Mac Studios generate over 36 tokens per second at an 8,192-token context.
items.why: It shows a path to run a frontier-size open model locally, without cloud GPU cost.

items.title: Deep dive: transformers as associative memory
items.body: Alex Wang explains linear layers, MLPs and self-attention as associative memory stores with similarity-weighted lookup. A plain outer-product store holds about as many memories as its key dimension. Squared-ReLU MLPs reach about 2,700 memories at a 64-dimensional key. Softmax attention can reach about 1.2 million.
items.why: It gives a clear mental model of attention and MLPs, which helps you reason about context limits in agents.

aws-news.headline: AWS publishes a nine-stage evaluation framework for production AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
aws-news.note: The AWS What's New page showed only loading placeholders, so the What's New RSS feed was used; it was a quiet weekend with no new Bedrock, ECS, EKS, IAM or Mumbai/Hyderabad launches.

items.title: AWS shares nine-stage evaluation playbook for AgentCore agents
items.body: An AWS Machine Learning blog post describes a nine-stage framework that runs from a golden test set through CI sentinel tests, CD quality gates, canary runs, guardrails, drift detection and a feedback loop. It uses AgentCore Evaluations, Observability, optimization, Gateway and runtime, plus Bedrock Guardrails and CloudWatch. In the AWS sales team rollout, pass rate rose from 93% to 96% and hallucinations fell from 138 to under 52 per 10,000 responses. Online evaluation samples 10% of live traffic, and dataset evaluation is in public preview.
items.why: It gives a ready CI/CD pattern to test, gate and monitor the quality of AI agents shipped on AWS.

items.title: Open-weight agentic coding model Reflection Beam lands on SageMaker
items.body: Reflection Beam is a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 501 billion total and 23 billion active parameters and a reported 1 million token context. The weights use the Apache 2.0 license and come in BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 versions. It is available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart in US East (N. Virginia) and US East (Ohio), and on SageMaker HyperPod Inference orchestrated by Amazon EKS. The post does not mention Amazon Bedrock and reports no benchmarks.
items.why: It is a self-hosted Apache 2.0 coding model that teams can compare with Claude Code for agent work on EKS.
